# Part 1: Setup and Study Context

## 1.1 Study context

Singapore is adding two rail lines. The Jurong Region Line (JRL) brings 24 stations to the West, and Cross Island Line (CRL) Phase 1 brings 12 stations across the north-east. Before they open, planners need to know which new stations will be busy, which existing stations will lose riders to them, and which neighbourhoods gain real access.

This study answers four questions:

1.  How well can a probabilistic station-choice (Huff) model explain average weekday entries at today's stations?
2.  How many entries should the JRL and CRL Phase 1 stations expect?
3.  Which existing stations lose catchment to the new lines, and where?
4.  How much closer to a station do HDB neighbourhoods become?

The original brief also asked about older residents. That analysis needs population by age, which is not in this study's data, so section 7.3 explains how it was handled.

## 1.2 Network context

The current network combines MRT lines and three LRT systems. Of the 36 proposed stations, 29 are new places to board. The other 7 are built at existing stations, so they are modelled as those stations gaining a line rather than as new choices. Section 2.2 builds and checks these counts from the data.

## 1.3 Load dependencies

`igraph` groups interchange polygons into stations, `MCI` provides a reference implementation of the Huff model for checking, and `leaflet` draws the interactive catchment map. `igraph` is loaded before `tidyverse` so that `dplyr` and `purrr` functions keep their usual names.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(igraph, sf, tmap, leaflet, MCI, knitr, scales, tidyverse)

svy21 <- 3414
data_dir <- "data"
od_dir <- "data"
rds_dir <- "data/rds"
dir.create(rds_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 0) label_comma(accuracy = 10^-digits)(x)
fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) label_percent(accuracy = 10^-digits)(x)
```

The figure helpers keep every chart consistent. Proposed stations are blue (new) or orange (upgraded), the existing network is grey, the two new lines are blue (JRL) and aqua (CRL), and magnitudes use a single blue ramp where darker means more.

```{r}
#| label: figure-helpers
report_colors <- c(
  "New alternative" = "#2a78d6",
  "Upgraded interchange" = "#eb6834",
  "Existing MRT" = "#898781",
  "Existing LRT" = "#c3c2b7",
  "Not yet open" = "#ffffff"
)
line_colors <- c(JRL = "#2a78d6", CRL = "#1baf7a")
ink <- "#0b0b0b"
ink_secondary <- "#52514e"
land <- "#f0efec"
blue_ramp <- c("#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b")

theme_report <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      axis.text = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
}

map_legend <- function(title) {
  tm_legend(title = title, position = tm_pos_out("right", "center"), frame = FALSE)
}

map_finish <- function() {
  tm_scalebar(position = c("right", "bottom"), breaks = c(0, 5, 10), text.size = 0.6) +
    tm_layout(frame = FALSE, inner.margins = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 0.02))
}
```

# Part 2: Data Ingestion and Cleaning

| Dataset | Location in `data/` | Used for |
|----|----|----|
| LTA passenger volume by origin-destination train station, Aug and Sep 2026 | `origin_destination_train/` (downloaded by `scripts/download_od.R`) | Average weekday entries and hourly profiles |
| LTA train stations, Sep 2026 | `TrainStation_Sep2026/` | Existing stations |
| Future station coordinates | `future_stations.csv` | Proposed stations |
| HDB existing buildings | `HDBExistingBuilding.geojson` | Residential demand |
| LTA bus stops, Sep 2026 | `BusStopLocation_Sep2026/` | Station attraction |
| OpenStreetMap (Geofabrik) | `malaysia-singapore-brunei-261106-free.shp/` | Boundaries, workplaces, points of interest, station names |

## 2.1 Origin-destination data

The monthly files come from DataMall's `PV/ODTrain` API, which needs a personal AccountKey and serves only the last three months. `scripts/download_od.R` downloads them into `data/origin_destination_train/`, reading the key from the `LTA_ACCOUNT_KEY` environment variable so that it never appears in this report.

Average weekday entries are total weekday tap-ins divided by the number of weekdays in each month. LTA counts public holidays with weekends, so National Day's observed holiday on Monday 10 August is excluded from August's weekdays. The calendar below needs no passenger data, so it always runs.

```{r}
#| label: calendar
public_holidays <- as.Date("2026-08-10")

day_counts <- function(year_month) {
  first_day <- ymd(paste0(year_month, "-01"))
  all_days <- seq(first_day, first_day + months(1) - days(1), by = "day")
  is_weekday <- wday(all_days, week_start = 1) <= 5 & !all_days %in% public_holidays
  tibble(
    year_month = year_month,
    weekdays = sum(is_weekday),
    weekend_or_holiday = sum(!is_weekday)
  )
}

od_files <- list.files(
  od_dir,
  pattern = "^origin_destination_train_2026(08|09)\\.(csv|zip)$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)
has_od <- length(od_files) > 0

od_months <- if (has_od) {
  str_extract(basename(od_files), "2026\\d{2}") |>
    str_replace("(\\d{4})(\\d{2})", "\\1-\\2")
} else {
  c("2026-08", "2026-09")
}

calendar <- map(od_months, day_counts) |> list_rbind()
n_weekdays <- sum(calendar$weekdays)
n_weekend_days <- sum(calendar$weekend_or_holiday)

kable(calendar, col.names = c("Month", "Weekdays", "Weekend or holiday days"))
```

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr "!has_od"
::: callout-warning
No `origin_destination_train_202608` or `_202609` file was found under `data/`. Steps that need observed entries (sections 2.1, 4, 5 and 6) are shown as code but not run. Everything else in this report runs from the files already present.
:::
```

Each row of the LTA file is a monthly total for one origin, destination, day type and hour. Entries are summed by origin code; destinations are not needed for station entries.

```{r}
#| label: read-od
#| eval: !expr has_od
od_raw <- map(
  od_files,
  \(file) read_csv(
    file,
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    col_types = cols(
      .default = col_character(),
      TIME_PER_HOUR = col_integer(),
      TOTAL_TRIPS = col_double()
    )
  )
) |>
  list_rbind()

origin_hourly_codes <- od_raw |>
  group_by(od_code = ORIGIN_PT_CODE, DAY_TYPE, TIME_PER_HOUR) |>
  summarise(trips = sum(TOTAL_TRIPS), .groups = "drop")

od_raw |>
  count(YEAR_MONTH, DAY_TYPE, wt = TOTAL_TRIPS, name = "trips") |>
  mutate(trips = fmt_num(trips)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Month", "Day type", "Trips"))
```

## 2.2 Stations and code standardisation

The LTA station layer uses SVY21 without an EPSG code, so the code is assigned rather than reprojected. Depots and facility buildings are removed by keeping only codes with a station number, plus `PTC` and `STC`, the two LRT interchange codes that have none.

```{r}
#| label: import-stations
station_raw <- st_read(
  file.path(data_dir, "TrainStation_Sep2026/RapidTransitSystemStation.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  st_set_crs(svy21) |>
  st_make_valid()

station_poly <- station_raw |>
  filter(str_detect(STN_NAM, "\\d") | STN_NAM %in% c("PTC", "STC")) |>
  group_by(poly_code = STN_NAM) |>
  summarise(.groups = "drop")

tibble(
  polygons_in_layer = nrow(station_raw),
  distinct_codes = n_distinct(station_raw$STN_NAM),
  passenger_codes = nrow(station_poly)
) |>
  kable()
```

Each physical station must be one choice, but interchange codes are stored as separate polygons. Polygons within 5 m of each other are treated as one station. A small tolerance is needed because Newton's two polygons (`NS21`, `DT11`) are separated by a sub-metre gap; any tolerance from 1 m to 20 m merges Newton and nothing else. Two interchanges do not touch and are linked by hand: Bukit Panjang (`BP6`, `DT1`) and Tampines (`DT32`, `EW2`). Distance alone cannot do this, because Bras Basah and Bencoolen are only 63 m apart yet are separate stations.

```{r}
#| label: group-interchanges
touching <- st_is_within_distance(station_poly, dist = 5) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(row.id < col.id) |>
  transmute(
    from = station_poly$poly_code[row.id],
    to = station_poly$poly_code[col.id]
  )

links <- bind_rows(
  touching,
  tribble(
    ~from, ~to,
    "BP6", "DT1",
    "DT32", "EW2"
  )
)

station_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  links,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = station_poly$poly_code
)
station_group <- igraph::components(station_graph)$membership
```

Codes are then standardised in three ways:

- Some polygons carry one code for two lines, such as `CC29` for HarbourFront, which is also `NE1`.
- Passenger data may label Marina Bay and Bayfront as `CC33` and `CC34`, while the station layer uses `CE2` and `CE1`. Both spellings are mapped to the same stations.
- The three Circle Line 6 stations, Keppel, Cantonment and Prince Edward Road (`CC30` to `CC32`), are in the station layer and are treated as open. The stations still flagged as not yet open are Bukit Brown, Mount Pleasant, Marina South and Founders' Memorial. Once passenger data is present, a station counts as open only if it records entries.

```{r}
#| label: station-lookup
hidden_codes <- tribble(
  ~poly_code, ~code,
  "CC17", "TE9",
  "CC29", "NE1",
  "CE2", "TE20",
  "DT10", "TE11",
  "EW16", "TE17",
  "NS22", "TE14"
)

renumbered_codes <- tribble(
  ~code, ~same_as,
  "CC33", "CE2",
  "CC34", "CE1"
)

not_open_codes <- c("CC18", "TE10", "TE21", "TE22A")

line_of <- function(code) {
  prefix <- str_extract(code, "^[A-Z]+")
  merged <- c(
    CG = "EW", CE = "CC",
    BP = "BPLRT",
    SE = "SLRT", SW = "SLRT", STC = "SLRT",
    PE = "PLRT", PW = "PLRT", PTC = "PLRT"
  )
  coalesce(unname(merged[prefix]), prefix)
}
lrt_lines <- c("BPLRT", "SLRT", "PLRT")

station_codes <- tibble(
  poly_code = station_poly$poly_code,
  group = station_group[station_poly$poly_code]
) |>
  mutate(code = poly_code) |>
  separate_rows(code, sep = "\\s*/\\s*") |>
  bind_rows(
    hidden_codes |>
      left_join(
        tibble(poly_code = names(station_group), group = station_group),
        by = "poly_code"
      )
  ) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(station_id = str_c(sort(unique(code)), collapse = "-")) |>
  ungroup()

code_lookup <- station_codes |>
  distinct(code, station_id)

code_lookup <- bind_rows(
  code_lookup,
  renumbered_codes |>
    inner_join(code_lookup, by = c(same_as = "code")) |>
    select(code, station_id)
)

station_summary <- station_codes |>
  mutate(line = line_of(code)) |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_lines_base = n_distinct(line),
    is_lrt = all(line %in% lrt_lines),
    provisionally_open = !any(code %in% not_open_codes),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

existing_poly <- station_poly |>
  left_join(distinct(station_codes, poly_code, station_id), by = "poly_code") |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(.groups = "drop")

write_rds(existing_poly, file.path(rds_dir, "existing_poly.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(code_lookup, file.path(rds_dir, "code_lookup.rds"), compress = "gz")

station_summary |>
  count(is_lrt, provisionally_open) |>
  kable(col.names = c("LRT only", "Treated as open", "Stations"))
```

The station layer has codes but no names. OpenStreetMap supplies a name wherever a mapped station lies within 150 m, which covers about a third of stations; the rest are labelled by code.

```{r}
#| label: station-names
osm_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "malaysia-singapore-brunei-261106-free.shp")
bbox_wkt <- "POLYGON((103.59 1.15, 104.10 1.15, 104.10 1.48, 103.59 1.48, 103.59 1.15))"

osm_station_names <- bind_rows(
  st_read(file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_transport_free_1.shp"), wkt_filter = bbox_wkt, quiet = TRUE) |>
    filter(fclass %in% c("railway_station", "railway_halt")) |>
    select(name),
  st_read(
    file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.shp"),
    query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1 WHERE type = 'train_station'",
    wkt_filter = bbox_wkt, quiet = TRUE
  ) |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_point_on_surface() |>
    select(name)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(name)) |>
  st_transform(svy21)

existing_points <- st_centroid(existing_poly)
nearest_name <- st_nearest_feature(existing_points, osm_station_names)
name_gap <- as.numeric(
  st_distance(existing_points, osm_station_names[nearest_name, ], by_element = TRUE)
)

station_names <- tibble(
  station_id = existing_poly$station_id,
  station_label = if_else(
    name_gap <= 150,
    str_c(osm_station_names$name[nearest_name], " (", station_id, ")"),
    station_id
  )
)

tibble(stations = nrow(station_names), named = sum(name_gap <= 150)) |>
  kable()
```

Weekday entries and hourly profiles are now linked to physical stations. An origin code such as `NE17-PTC` is split into its parts, and every part must point to the same station.

```{r}
#| label: link-od
#| eval: !expr has_od
od_station <- origin_hourly_codes |>
  distinct(od_code) |>
  mutate(code = od_code) |>
  separate_rows(code, sep = "[-/\\s]+") |>
  left_join(code_lookup, by = "code")

ambiguous_codes <- od_station |>
  filter(!is.na(station_id)) |>
  distinct(od_code, station_id) |>
  count(od_code) |>
  filter(n > 1)
stopifnot(nrow(ambiguous_codes) == 0)

od_station <- od_station |>
  filter(!is.na(station_id)) |>
  distinct(od_code, station_id)

unmatched_codes <- setdiff(unique(origin_hourly_codes$od_code), od_station$od_code)

station_hourly <- origin_hourly_codes |>
  inner_join(od_station, by = "od_code") |>
  group_by(station_id, DAY_TYPE, TIME_PER_HOUR) |>
  summarise(trips = sum(trips), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    avg_entries = if_else(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY", trips / n_weekdays, trips / n_weekend_days)
  )

entries <- station_hourly |>
  filter(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY") |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(avg_weekday_entries = sum(avg_entries), .groups = "drop")

write_rds(station_hourly, file.path(rds_dir, "station_hourly.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(entries, file.path(rds_dir, "entries.rds"), compress = "gz")

tibble(
  origin_codes = n_distinct(origin_hourly_codes$od_code),
  unmatched = length(unmatched_codes),
  stations_with_entries = nrow(entries)
) |>
  kable()
```

## 2.3 Proposed stations

Only the 36 stations in the brief are kept. A proposed station within 100 m of an existing station is an upgraded interchange rather than a new choice.

```{r}
#| label: proposed-stations
proposed_codes <- c(
  paste0("JS", 1:12), paste0("JE", 1:7), paste0("JW", 1:5), paste0("CR", 2:13)
)

proposed <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "future_stations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(station_code %in% proposed_codes) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(svy21) |>
  mutate(line = if_else(str_starts(station_code, "CR"), "CRL", "JRL"))

nearest_existing <- st_nearest_feature(proposed, existing_poly)

proposed <- proposed |>
  mutate(
    host_station = existing_poly$station_id[nearest_existing],
    gap_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry, existing_poly[nearest_existing, ], by_element = TRUE)
    ),
    proposed_type = if_else(gap_m <= 100, "upgraded_interchange", "new_alternative")
  )

stopifnot(nrow(proposed) == 36)
stopifnot(sum(proposed$proposed_type == "upgraded_interchange") == 7)

write_rds(proposed, file.path(rds_dir, "proposed.rds"), compress = "gz")

proposed |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(line, proposed_type) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Line", "Type", "Stations"))
```

## 2.4 Geographic boundaries

OpenStreetMap's national polygon follows the maritime boundary, so it includes open sea and distant Pedra Branca. The administrative areas inside it follow the coast instead. Level 6 holds the 55 planning areas and level 7 holds 331 subzones, which stand in for the URA Master Plan subzones. The SingStat population tables are not part of this study's data, so no demographic attributes are merged.

```{r}
#| label: boundaries
admin_areas <- st_read(file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_adminareas_a_free_1.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(svy21)

national <- admin_areas |>
  filter(fclass == "national", name == "Singapore")

inside_singapore <- function(areas) {
  areas[lengths(st_within(st_point_on_surface(areas), national)) > 0, ]
}

planning_areas <- admin_areas |>
  filter(fclass == "admin_level6") |>
  inside_singapore() |>
  select(planning_area = name)

subzones <- admin_areas |>
  filter(fclass == "admin_level7") |>
  inside_singapore() |>
  transmute(subzone_id = as.character(osm_id), subzone = name)

subzone_planning_area <- st_point_on_surface(subzones) |>
  st_join(planning_areas) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(subzone_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(subzone_id, planning_area)

subzones <- subzones |>
  left_join(subzone_planning_area, by = "subzone_id")

singapore <- st_union(planning_areas)

stopifnot(nrow(planning_areas) == 55)

write_rds(planning_areas, file.path(rds_dir, "planning_areas.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(subzones, file.path(rds_dir, "subzones.rds"), compress = "gz")

tibble(
  n_planning_areas = nrow(planning_areas),
  n_subzones = nrow(subzones),
  n_with_planning_area = sum(!is.na(subzones$planning_area))
) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Planning areas", "Subzones", "Subzones with a planning area"))

map_base <- function() {
  tm_shape(planning_areas) +
    tm_polygons(fill = land, col = "#d9d8d0", lwd = 0.4)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-network
#| fig-cap: "Existing rail network and the 36 proposed stations"
#| fig-alt: "Map of Singapore showing existing MRT and LRT stations in grey, stations not yet open as hollow markers, 29 new stations in blue and 7 upgraded interchanges in orange."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
class_order <- c(
  "Not yet open", "Existing LRT", "Existing MRT",
  "Upgraded interchange", "New alternative"
)

network_points <- bind_rows(
  existing_points |>
    left_join(station_summary, by = "station_id") |>
    transmute(
      map_class = case_when(
        !provisionally_open ~ "Not yet open",
        is_lrt ~ "Existing LRT",
        TRUE ~ "Existing MRT"
      )
    ),
  proposed |>
    transmute(
      map_class = if_else(
        proposed_type == "new_alternative", "New alternative", "Upgraded interchange"
      )
    )
) |>
  mutate(map_class = factor(map_class, levels = class_order)) |>
  arrange(map_class)

map_base() +
  tm_shape(network_points) +
  tm_symbols(
    fill = "map_class",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = unname(report_colors[class_order])),
    fill.legend = map_legend("Station"),
    shape = "map_class",
    shape.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c(21, 21, 21, 23, 21)),
    shape.legend = tm_legend_combine("fill"),
    size = "map_class",
    size.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c(0.35, 0.3, 0.4, 0.75, 0.6)),
    size.legend = tm_legend_combine("fill"),
    col = ink_secondary,
    lwd = 0.5
  ) +
  map_finish()
```

The JRL forms a branching cluster in the West, and CRL Phase 1 runs across the north-east. Of the 36 proposed stations, 29 are new places to board (blue) and 7 share a site with an existing station (orange). Hollow markers are stations in the LTA layer that have not opened.

```{r}
#| label: fig-gap
#| fig-cap: "Distance from each proposed station to its nearest existing station"
#| fig-alt: "Dot plot of 36 proposed stations ranked by distance to the nearest existing station. Seven sit within 100 metres; every other station is at least 578 metres away."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7.5
proposed |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    type = if_else(
      proposed_type == "new_alternative", "New alternative", "Upgraded interchange"
    ),
    station_label = fct_reorder(str_c(station_name, " (", station_code, ")"), gap_m)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gap_m, y = station_label, color = type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, color = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 130, y = 2.5, label = "100 m threshold",
    hjust = 0, size = 3.2, color = ink_secondary
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = report_colors[c("New alternative", "Upgraded interchange")]) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest existing station (m)", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

The seven co-located stations are no more than 78 m from an existing station, and the next closest is 578 m away, so any threshold in between gives the same split.

# Part 3: Spatial Feature Engineering

## 3.1 Residential demand

Each HDB building is a residential origin, placed at its own centroid rather than at a subzone centre. The intended weight was the number of residents per block, from HDB property records and SingStat population. Neither is in this study's data, so each building is weighted by its footprint area instead. This treats blocks of different heights alike and cannot exclude non-residential HDB buildings.

```{r}
#| label: homes
assign_subzone <- function(points) {
  joined <- st_join(points, subzones |> select(subzone_id, subzone, planning_area))
  missing <- is.na(joined$subzone_id)
  if (any(missing)) {
    nearest <- st_nearest_feature(joined[missing, ], subzones)
    joined$subzone_id[missing] <- subzones$subzone_id[nearest]
    joined$subzone[missing] <- subzones$subzone[nearest]
    joined$planning_area[missing] <- subzones$planning_area[nearest]
  }
  joined
}

homes <- st_read(file.path(data_dir, "HDBExistingBuilding.geojson"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(svy21) |>
  transmute(
    origin_id = str_c("H", POSTAL_COD),
    origin_type = "home",
    home_m2 = SHAPE.AREA,
    work_floor_m2 = 0,
    poi_count = 0
  ) |>
  st_centroid() |>
  assign_subzone()

write_rds(homes, file.path(rds_dir, "homes.rds"), compress = "gz")

homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    buildings = n(),
    subzones_with_hdb = n_distinct(subzone_id),
    footprint_ha = sum(home_m2) / 1e4
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-home-subzones
#| fig-cap: "HDB building footprint by subzone"
#| fig-alt: "Choropleth of Singapore subzones in which darker blue means more HDB building footprint. Footprint concentrates in the housing towns."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
home_subzones <- homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(subzone_id) |>
  summarise(footprint_ha = sum(home_m2) / 1e4, .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(x = subzones, by = "subzone_id")

map_base() +
  tm_shape(home_subzones) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "footprint_ha",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
      breaks = c(0, 4, 7, 11, 16, Inf),
      values = blue_ramp,
      labels = c("Under 4", "4 to 7", "7 to 11", "11 to 16", "16 or more")
    ),
    fill.legend = map_legend("HDB footprint (ha)"),
    col = "white",
    lwd = 0.3
  ) +
  map_finish()
```

HDB footprint is concentrated in the housing towns, such as Tampines, Jurong West, Woodlands and Sengkang, with little in the centre and the industrial west. These towns are where most residential demand for stations comes from.

## 3.2 Activity and workplace demand

People also board near where they work, study and shop. SingStat worker counts are not available, so two OpenStreetMap measures stand in for them:

- Workplace floor area, from the footprints of office, commercial, retail, industrial, warehouse, hotel, hospital and education buildings.
- Activity, a count of shops, food outlets, services and schools.

Both are summed into 500 m grid cells, and each cell with any activity becomes a workplace origin at its centre.

```{r}
#| label: workplaces
work_types <- c(
  "office", "commercial", "retail", "industrial", "warehouse", "hotel",
  "hospital", "school", "university", "college", "data_center"
)

work_buildings <- st_read(
  file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.shp"),
  query = str_c(
    "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1 WHERE type IN ('",
    str_c(work_types, collapse = "','"), "')"
  ),
  wkt_filter = bbox_wkt,
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_transform(svy21)

work_buildings$floor_m2 <- as.numeric(st_area(work_buildings))

work_buildings <- work_buildings |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  st_filter(singapore) |>
  select(type, floor_m2)

poi_classes <- list(
  retail = c(
    "mall", "department_store", "supermarket", "convenience", "marketplace",
    "clothes", "shoe_shop", "jeweller", "optician", "beauty_shop",
    "hairdresser", "bakery", "greengrocer", "butcher", "florist", "gift_shop",
    "bookshop", "stationery", "toy_shop", "sports_shop", "mobile_phone_shop",
    "computer_shop", "furniture_shop", "doityourself", "chemist", "general",
    "kiosk", "beverages", "newsagent", "video_shop", "outdoor_shop",
    "garden_centre", "bicycle_shop", "laundry"
  ),
  food = c("restaurant", "cafe", "fast_food", "food_court", "bar", "pub"),
  services = c(
    "bank", "clinic", "doctors", "dentist", "pharmacy", "hospital",
    "post_office", "library", "community_centre", "fitness_centre", "veterinary"
  ),
  education = c("school", "kindergarten", "college", "university")
)

pois <- bind_rows(
  st_read(file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_pois_free_1.shp"), wkt_filter = bbox_wkt, quiet = TRUE),
  st_read(file.path(osm_dir, "gis_osm_pois_a_free_1.shp"), wkt_filter = bbox_wkt, quiet = TRUE) |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_transform(svy21) |>
    st_point_on_surface() |>
    st_transform(4326)
) |>
  filter(fclass %in% unlist(poi_classes, use.names = FALSE)) |>
  distinct(osm_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(svy21) |>
  st_filter(singapore) |>
  select(osm_id, fclass)

grid_500 <- st_make_grid(singapore, cellsize = 500, square = TRUE) |>
  st_sf(geometry = _) |>
  mutate(cell_id = row_number())

cell_of <- function(points) {
  st_join(points, grid_500, join = st_intersects) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    distinct(.keep_all = TRUE)
}

cell_activity <- full_join(
  cell_of(work_buildings) |>
    group_by(cell_id) |>
    summarise(work_floor_m2 = sum(floor_m2), .groups = "drop"),
  cell_of(pois) |>
    count(cell_id, name = "poi_count"),
  by = "cell_id"
) |>
  mutate(across(c(work_floor_m2, poi_count), \(x) coalesce(x, 0)))

workplaces <- grid_500 |>
  inner_join(cell_activity, by = "cell_id") |>
  st_centroid() |>
  transmute(
    origin_id = str_c("W", cell_id),
    origin_type = "work",
    home_m2 = 0,
    work_floor_m2,
    poi_count
  ) |>
  assign_subzone()

write_rds(work_buildings, file.path(rds_dir, "work_buildings.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(pois, file.path(rds_dir, "pois.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(workplaces, file.path(rds_dir, "workplaces.rds"), compress = "gz")

workplaces |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    cells = n(),
    workplace_floor_ha = sum(work_floor_m2) / 1e4,
    pois = sum(poi_count)
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-workplaces
#| fig-cap: "Workplace floor area per 500 m cell"
#| fig-alt: "Grid map of Singapore in which darker blue means more office, commercial, industrial and institutional floor area. The largest values are in the city centre and the western industrial estates."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
map_base() +
  tm_shape(grid_500 |> inner_join(cell_activity |> filter(work_floor_m2 > 0), by = "cell_id")) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "work_floor_m2",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
      breaks = c(0, 3000, 8000, 15000, 30000, Inf),
      values = blue_ramp,
      labels = c("Under 3,000", "3,000 to 8,000", "8,000 to 15,000", "15,000 to 30,000", "30,000 or more")
    ),
    fill.legend = map_legend("Workplace floor (m²)"),
    col = "white",
    lwd = 0.2
  ) +
  map_finish()
```

Workplace floor area peaks in the city centre and the western industrial estates around Jurong and Tuas, a very different pattern from housing. A station in an industrial estate can therefore attract workers even if few people live nearby.

```{r}
#| label: fig-demand-mix
#| fig-cap: "Share of residential and workplace demand by planning area"
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell chart of the 15 planning areas with the most demand. Each row compares the area's share of Singapore's HDB footprint with its share of workplace floor area."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
demand_mix <- bind_rows(
  homes |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(planning_area) |>
    summarise(value = sum(home_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(measure = "Residential footprint"),
  workplaces |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(planning_area) |>
    summarise(value = sum(work_floor_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(measure = "Workplace floor area")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(planning_area)) |>
  group_by(measure) |>
  mutate(share = value / sum(value)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  complete(planning_area, measure, fill = list(value = 0, share = 0))

top_demand_areas <- demand_mix |>
  group_by(planning_area) |>
  summarise(largest_share = max(share), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(largest_share, n = 15) |>
  pull(planning_area)

demand_order <- demand_mix |>
  filter(planning_area %in% top_demand_areas, measure == "Residential footprint") |>
  arrange(share) |>
  pull(planning_area)

demand_mix |>
  filter(planning_area %in% top_demand_areas) |>
  mutate(planning_area = factor(planning_area, levels = demand_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = planning_area)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = planning_area), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = measure), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Residential footprint" = "#2a78d6", "Workplace floor area" = "#eb6834")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "Share of Singapore total", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Homes and workplaces sit in different places. Housing towns such as Tampines, Punggol and Yishun hold a much larger share of HDB footprint than of workplace floor area. Tuas and Pioneer have no HDB at all, yet together hold about a seventh of the workplace floor area. A model that knew only where people live would miss stations serving these industrial estates, which matters for JRL stations such as Tukang and Jurong Pier.

## 3.3 Station features

Every candidate station gets its line count, whether it is LRT-only, and the number of bus stops within 400 m, 500 m and 800 m of its centre. Bus stops come from the September 2026 layer, so counts around proposed stations reflect today's bus network.

Feeder buses matter only if riders can reach the stop, so each radius stands for a different walking threshold:

- 400 m is about a five-minute walk, the distance commonly used for how far people will walk to a bus stop. It counts the stops right at the station.
- 500 m is a slightly wider ring that captures stops just beyond the station's immediate street block. It tests whether the result is sensitive to a small change in radius.
- 800 m is about a ten-minute walk, the same threshold this report uses for station coverage in Part 7. It counts the wider feeder network around a station.

The model does not assume which radius is right. Section 5.2 fits it with each count and keeps the one that matches observed entries best.

```{r}
#| label: station-features
bus_stops <- st_read(file.path(data_dir, "BusStopLocation_Sep2026/BusStop.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_set_crs(svy21)

write_rds(bus_stops, file.path(rds_dir, "bus_stops.rds"), compress = "gz")

upgrades <- proposed |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(proposed_type == "upgraded_interchange") |>
  transmute(station_id = host_station, upgrade_line = line, upgraded_by = station_code)

existing_master <- existing_points |>
  left_join(station_summary, by = "station_id") |>
  left_join(station_names, by = "station_id") |>
  left_join(upgrades, by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(station_type = "existing", line = NA_character_)

existing_master <- if (has_od) {
  existing_master |>
    left_join(entries, by = "station_id") |>
    mutate(operating = coalesce(avg_weekday_entries, 0) > 0)
} else {
  existing_master |>
    mutate(avg_weekday_entries = NA_real_, operating = provisionally_open)
}

new_master <- proposed |>
  filter(proposed_type == "new_alternative") |>
  transmute(
    station_id = station_code,
    station_label = str_c(station_name, " (", station_code, ")"),
    station_type = "new_alternative",
    line,
    is_lrt = FALSE,
    n_lines_base = 1L,
    upgrade_line = NA_character_,
    upgraded_by = NA_character_,
    avg_weekday_entries = NA_real_,
    operating = FALSE
  )

stations <- bind_rows(
  existing_master |>
    select(station_id, station_label, station_type, line, is_lrt, n_lines_base,
           upgrade_line, upgraded_by, avg_weekday_entries, operating),
  new_master
) |>
  mutate(
    in_baseline = station_type == "existing" & operating,
    bus_400 = lengths(st_is_within_distance(geometry, bus_stops, 400)),
    bus_500 = lengths(st_is_within_distance(geometry, bus_stops, 500)),
    bus_800 = lengths(st_is_within_distance(geometry, bus_stops, 800))
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(stations$station_id))
stopifnot(sum(stations$station_type == "new_alternative") == 29)

write_rds(stations, file.path(rds_dir, "stations.rds"), compress = "gz")

stations |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(station_type, in_baseline) |>
  summarise(
    stations = n(),
    median_bus_400 = median(bus_400),
    median_bus_800 = median(bus_800),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable()
```

Counts at neighbouring radii overlap heavily, because every stop within 400 m is also within 500 m and 800 m. The rank correlations below show how much each radius adds.

```{r}
#| label: bus-radius-correlation
bus_correlation <- stations |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(in_baseline) |>
  select(`400 m` = bus_400, `500 m` = bus_500, `800 m` = bus_800) |>
  cor(method = "spearman")

bus_correlation |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "Radius") |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

The 400 m and 500 m counts rank stations almost identically (correlation `r round(bus_correlation["400 m", "500 m"], 2)`), so 500 m mainly confirms the 400 m result. The 800 m count is more distinct (`r round(bus_correlation["400 m", "800 m"], 2)` with 400 m), because it reaches the wider feeder network.

Each network scenario is a set of stations with their line counts. A scenario that adds a line also adds one line to the existing stations that line upgrades. Switching `uplift` off removes that extra line, which section 6.5 uses as a sensitivity test.

```{r}
#| label: scenarios
scenario_lines <- list(
  existing = character(0),
  jrl = "JRL",
  crl = "CRL",
  both = c("JRL", "CRL")
)

scenario_labels <- c(
  existing = "Existing network",
  jrl = "JRL added",
  crl = "CRL Phase 1 added",
  both = "Both lines added"
)

scenario_destinations <- function(scenario, uplift = TRUE) {
  added <- scenario_lines[[scenario]]
  stations |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(in_baseline | (station_type == "new_alternative" & line %in% added)) |>
    mutate(
      n_lines = n_lines_base +
        as.integer(uplift & !is.na(upgrade_line) & upgrade_line %in% added)
    )
}

map(names(scenario_lines), \(s) {
  dest <- scenario_destinations(s)
  tibble(
    scenario = scenario_labels[[s]],
    stations = nrow(dest),
    new_stations = sum(dest$station_type == "new_alternative"),
    upgraded = sum(dest$n_lines > dest$n_lines_base)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bus
#| fig-cap: "Bus stops near existing and proposed stations"
#| fig-alt: "Strip plots of bus stops within 400, 500 and 800 metres for new stations, upgraded interchanges and other existing stations. A vertical bar marks each group's median."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
bus_data <- stations |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(in_baseline | station_type == "new_alternative") |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      station_type == "new_alternative" ~ "New alternative",
      !is.na(upgraded_by) ~ "Upgraded interchange",
      TRUE ~ "Other existing station"
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("New alternative", "Upgraded interchange", "Other existing station"))
  ) |>
  select(group, `Within 400 m` = bus_400, `Within 500 m` = bus_500, `Within 800 m` = bus_800) |>
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "radius", values_to = "bus_stops")

bus_median <- bus_data |>
  group_by(group, radius) |>
  summarise(median_stops = median(bus_stops), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(bus_data, aes(x = bus_stops, y = group, color = group)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.2, seed = 626), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(
    data = bus_median, aes(x = median_stops, y = group),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = "|", size = 9, color = ink
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~radius, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "New alternative" = unname(report_colors["New alternative"]),
      "Upgraded interchange" = unname(report_colors["Upgraded interchange"]),
      "Other existing station" = unname(report_colors["Existing MRT"])
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = "Bus stops (bar shows the median)", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

At every radius, new stations have fewer nearby bus stops than existing ones, and upgraded interchanges have the most. Bus routes are usually redesigned when a line opens, so today's counts understate the feeder access proposed stations will eventually have.

## 3.4 Spatial interactions

Every origin, residential and workplace, is paired with every candidate station. Straight-line distances are floored at 100 m, because a power distance-decay function grows without limit as distance approaches zero. Distances are stored as whole metres in an origin-by-station matrix, which the model reads directly.

```{r}
#| label: distance-matrix
origins <- bind_rows(homes, workplaces)
origin_xy <- st_coordinates(origins)
station_xy <- st_coordinates(stations)

dist_mat <- sqrt(
  outer(origin_xy[, "X"], station_xy[, "X"], "-")^2 +
    outer(origin_xy[, "Y"], station_xy[, "Y"], "-")^2
)
dist_mat <- round(pmax(dist_mat, 100))
storage.mode(dist_mat) <- "integer"
dimnames(dist_mat) <- list(origins$origin_id, stations$station_id)

write_rds(origins, file.path(rds_dir, "origins.rds"), compress = "gz")
write_rds(dist_mat, file.path(rds_dir, "dist_mat.rds"), compress = "gz")

tibble(
  residential_origins = sum(origins$origin_type == "home"),
  workplace_origins = sum(origins$origin_type == "work"),
  candidate_stations = ncol(dist_mat),
  origin_station_pairs = length(dist_mat)
) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), fmt_num)) |>
  kable()
```

The brief's spatial interaction data frame (origin, destination, attraction and distance) is the same matrix in long form. `sim_frame()` builds it for any scenario; the first rows for the existing network are shown below.

```{r}
#| label: sim-frame
sim_frame <- function(scenario, uplift = TRUE) {
  dest <- scenario_destinations(scenario, uplift)
  as_tibble(dist_mat[, dest$station_id], rownames = "origin_id") |>
    pivot_longer(-origin_id, names_to = "station_id", values_to = "distance_m") |>
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(origins) |> select(origin_id, origin_type, home_m2, work_floor_m2, poi_count), by = "origin_id") |>
    left_join(dest |> select(station_id, n_lines, is_lrt, bus_400, bus_500, bus_800), by = "station_id")
}

sim_existing <- sim_frame("existing")
nrow(sim_existing)
head(sim_existing) |> kable()
```

```{r}
  filter(in_baseline)

busiest <- baseline_stations |>

map_base() +

  tm_symbols(
```

```{r}
#| label: entries-commentary
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
top_station <- busiest |> slice_max(avg_weekday_entries, n = 1)
median_entries <- median(baseline_stations$avg_weekday_entries)

cat(str_glue(
  "The {nrow(baseline_stations)} operating stations record ",
  "{fmt_num(sum(baseline_stations$avg_weekday_entries))} entries on an average weekday. ",

))
```

## 4.2 Station diagnostics

Total entries hide when people travel. A station whose entries peak in the weekday evening is mainly a workplace stop, and one with steady use all week serves its neighbourhood. Raffles Place and Marine Parade show the two patterns.

```{r}
#| label: fig-profiles
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Hourly entries at a CBD station and a neighbourhood station"
#| fig-alt: "Two line charts of average entries by hour. Raffles Place has a sharp weekday evening peak; Marine Parade has a flatter pattern, with weekend use closer to weekday use."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
profile_ids <- code_lookup |>
  filter(code %in% c("EW14", "TE26")) |>
  mutate(profile = if_else(code == "EW14", "Raffles Place (CBD)", "Marine Parade (neighbourhood)"))

station_hourly |>
  inner_join(profile_ids, by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(day_type = if_else(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY", "Average weekday", "Average weekend or holiday")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = TIME_PER_HOUR, y = avg_entries, color = day_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~profile, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Average weekday" = "#2a78d6", "Average weekend or holiday" = "#eb6834")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Hour of entry", y = "Entries per day") +
  theme_report()
```

Ranking every station by its share of weekday entries between 17:00 and 19:59 finds the other workplace stations.

```{r}
#| label: evening-share
#| eval: !expr has_od
evening_share <- station_hourly |>
  filter(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY") |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(
    weekday_entries = sum(avg_entries),
    evening_share = sum(avg_entries[TIME_PER_HOUR %in% 17:19]) / weekday_entries,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(weekday_entries >= 1000) |>
  left_join(station_names, by = "station_id")

bind_rows(
  slice_max(evening_share, evening_share, n = 5) |> mutate(group = "Highest evening share"),
  slice_min(evening_share, evening_share, n = 5) |> mutate(group = "Lowest evening share")
) |>
  transmute(group, station = station_label, weekday_entries = fmt_num(weekday_entries), evening_share = fmt_pct(evening_share)) |>
  kable()
```

Evening-peak stations draw riders from workplaces, not homes. A model built only on housing would underpredict them, which is why section 5 tests workplace and activity measures as extra demand.

# Part 5: Huff Model Calibration and Validation

## 5.1 Attraction rules and model functions

A rider at origin $i$ chooses station $j$ with probability

$$P_{ij} = \frac{A_j \, d_{ij}^{-\lambda}}{\sum_k A_k \, d_{ik}^{-\lambda}},
\qquad
A_j = L_j^{\gamma_L} \, (B_j + 1)^{\gamma_B} \, e^{\delta R_j}$$

where $d_{ij}$ is the floored distance, $L_j$ the number of lines, $B_j$ the bus stops nearby, and $R_j$ is 1 for an LRT-only station. Adding one to the bus count keeps a station with no bus stops from having zero attraction, and the LRT indicator sits in an exponent for the same reason.

Predicted entries are $\hat{T}_j = \kappa \sum_i M_i P_{ij}$, where the demand $M_i$ is a residential origin's footprint, or a workplace origin's floor area times $\omega_F$ plus its activity count times $\omega_P$. Because $\kappa$ only rescales, it is solved directly so that predicted and observed totals match. The model therefore assumes a fixed total of trips: new stations take riders from existing ones instead of generating more.

```{r}
#| label: model-functions
huff_shares <- function(log_dist, log_attraction, lambda) {
  kernel <- exp(-lambda * log_dist + rep(log_attraction, each = nrow(log_dist)))
  kernel / rowSums(kernel)
}

log_attraction <- function(theta, dest, spec, bus_col = "bus_400") {
  if (!spec$use_attraction) return(rep(0, nrow(dest)))
  theta[["gamma_lines"]] * log(dest$n_lines) +
    theta[["gamma_bus"]] * log1p(dest[[bus_col]]) +
    theta[["delta_lrt"]] * dest$is_lrt
}

demand_vector <- function(theta, spec) {
  m <- origins$home_m2
  if (spec$use_floor) m <- m + exp(theta[["log_w_floor"]]) * origins$work_floor_m2
  if (spec$use_poi) m <- m + exp(theta[["log_w_poi"]]) * origins$poi_count
  m
}

station_scores <- function(theta, spec, dest, log_dist, bus_col = "bus_400") {
  shares <- huff_shares(log_dist, log_attraction(theta, dest, spec, bus_col), theta[["lambda"]])
  drop(crossprod(shares, demand_vector(theta, spec)))
}

poisson_deviance <- function(observed, fitted) {
  2 * sum(if_else(observed > 0, observed * log(observed / fitted), 0) - (observed - fitted))
}

wape <- function(observed, predicted) sum(abs(observed - predicted)) / sum(observed)

model_specs <- tribble(
  ~model, ~label, ~use_attraction, ~use_floor, ~use_poi,
  "M0", "Distance only", FALSE, FALSE, FALSE,
  "M1", "Station features", TRUE, FALSE, FALSE,
  "M2", "+ workplace floor area", TRUE, TRUE, FALSE,
  "M3", "+ workplace floor area and activity", TRUE, TRUE, TRUE
)

spec_of <- function(model_name) as.list(filter(model_specs, model == model_name))
```

Before fitting, the implementation is checked against `MCI::huff.shares()` for 25 residential origins and illustrative parameters. The two should agree to rounding error.

```{r}
#| label: mci-check
set.seed(626)
check_dest <- scenario_destinations("existing")
check_origins <- sample(origins$origin_id[origins$origin_type == "home"], 25)
check_theta <- c(lambda = 2, gamma_lines = 0.5, gamma_bus = 0.3, delta_lrt = -0.2)
check_attraction <- exp(log_attraction(check_theta, check_dest, spec_of("M1")))

our_shares <- huff_shares(
  log(dist_mat[check_origins, check_dest$station_id, drop = FALSE]),
  log(check_attraction),
  check_theta[["lambda"]]
)

mci_input <- expand_grid(origin = check_origins, location = check_dest$station_id) |>
  mutate(
    attrac = check_attraction[match(location, check_dest$station_id)],
    dist = dist_mat[cbind(origin, location)]
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()

mci_shares <- huff.shares(
  mci_input, "origin", "location", "attrac", "dist",
  gamma = 1, lambda = -check_theta[["lambda"]]
)

max_difference <- max(abs(
  mci_shares$p_ij - our_shares[cbind(match(mci_shares$origin, check_origins), match(mci_shares$location, check_dest$station_id))]
))

stopifnot(max_difference < 1e-9)
tibble(origin_station_pairs = nrow(mci_shares), max_difference = signif(max_difference, 2)) |>
  kable()
```

## 5.2 Fitting

Parameters are estimated with `optim()` by minimising the Poisson deviance between observed and predicted weekday entries, within bounds that keep decay positive. Four models are compared:

- M0 uses distance only, with every station equally attractive.
- M1 adds station features.
- M2 adds workplace floor area as demand.
- M3 adds activity as well, standing in for worker counts.

```{r}
#| label: fit-functions
param_start <- function(spec) {
  p <- c(lambda = 1.5)
  if (spec$use_attraction) p <- c(p, gamma_lines = 0.5, gamma_bus = 0.3, delta_lrt = 0)
  if (spec$use_floor) p <- c(p, log_w_floor = 0)
  if (spec$use_poi) p <- c(p, log_w_poi = log(500))
  p
}

param_bounds <- function(p, side) {
  lower <- c(lambda = 0.05, gamma_lines = -3, gamma_bus = -3, delta_lrt = -5, log_w_floor = -15, log_w_poi = -15)
  upper <- c(lambda = 6, gamma_lines = 3, gamma_bus = 3, delta_lrt = 5, log_w_floor = 15, log_w_poi = 15)
  if (side == "lower") lower[names(p)] else upper[names(p)]
}

fit_huff <- function(spec, observed, dest, log_dist, train = rep(TRUE, length(observed)),
                     start = NULL, bus_col = "bus_400") {
  p0 <- if (is.null(start)) param_start(spec) else start
  objective <- function(theta) {
    names(theta) <- names(p0)
    s <- station_scores(theta, spec, dest, log_dist, bus_col)
    kappa <- sum(observed[train]) / sum(s[train])
    poisson_deviance(observed[train], kappa * s[train])
  }
  opt <- optim(
    p0, objective,
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = param_bounds(p0, "lower"),
    upper = param_bounds(p0, "upper")
  )
  theta <- setNames(opt$par, names(p0))
  scores <- station_scores(theta, spec, dest, log_dist, bus_col)
  kappa <- sum(observed[train]) / sum(scores[train])
  list(
    theta = theta, kappa = kappa, fitted = kappa * scores,
    deviance = opt$value, convergence = opt$convergence, bus_col = bus_col
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-models
#| eval: !expr has_od
dest_existing <- scenario_destinations("existing")
log_dist_existing <- log(dist_mat[, dest_existing$station_id])
observed <- dest_existing$avg_weekday_entries

bus_choice <- map(c("bus_400", "bus_500", "bus_800"), \(b) {
  fit <- fit_huff(spec_of("M1"), observed, dest_existing, log_dist_existing, bus_col = b)
  tibble(bus_col = b, deviance = fit$deviance)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

bus_col <- bus_choice$bus_col[which.min(bus_choice$deviance)]

fits <- map(set_names(model_specs$model), \(m) {
  fit_huff(spec_of(m), observed, dest_existing, log_dist_existing, bus_col = bus_col)
})

bus_choice |>
  mutate(deviance = fmt_num(deviance), chosen = bus_col == .env$bus_col) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Bus radius", "M1 deviance", "Chosen"))
```

```{r}
#| label: bus-choice-commentary
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
deviance_spread <- (max(bus_choice$deviance) - min(bus_choice$deviance)) / min(bus_choice$deviance)

cat(str_glue(
  "The bus-stop radius is chosen by fit rather than assumed. The three radii give deviances within ",
  "{fmt_pct(deviance_spread)} of each other, and {str_remove(bus_col, 'bus_')} m fits best, so the choice ",
  "of radius has little effect on the results. That is expected from the high correlation between the ",
  "counts in section 3.3."
))
```

## 5.3 Five-fold geographic cross-validation

Stations are split into five geographic groups by k-means on their coordinates. Each model is refitted on four groups and predicts the fifth. Held-out stations stay in every rider's choice set, because riders can still choose them; only their entries are hidden from the fit.

```{r}
#| label: cross-validation
#| eval: !expr has_od
set.seed(626)
station_coords <- st_coordinates(stations)[match(dest_existing$station_id, stations$station_id), ]
fold <- kmeans(station_coords, centers = 5, nstart = 25)$cluster

cv_runs <- map(set_names(model_specs$model), \(m) {
  predicted <- numeric(length(observed))
  fold_thetas <- vector("list", 5)
  for (k in 1:5) {
    fold_fit <- fit_huff(
      spec_of(m), observed, dest_existing, log_dist_existing,
      train = fold != k, start = fits[[m]]$theta, bus_col = bus_col
    )
    predicted[fold == k] <- fold_fit$fitted[fold == k]
    fold_thetas[[k]] <- tibble(fold = k, parameter = names(fold_fit$theta), value = unname(fold_fit$theta))
  }
  list(predicted = predicted, thetas = list_rbind(fold_thetas))
})

cv_predictions <- map(cv_runs, "predicted")
fold_parameters <- imap(cv_runs, \(run, m) mutate(run$thetas, model = m)) |>
  list_rbind()

model_comparison <- model_specs |>
  transmute(
    model, label,
    parameters = map_int(model, \(m) length(fits[[m]]$theta)),
    lambda = map_dbl(model, \(m) fits[[m]]$theta[["lambda"]]),
    in_sample_wape = map_dbl(model, \(m) wape(observed, fits[[m]]$fitted)),
    cv_wape = map_dbl(model, \(m) wape(observed, cv_predictions[[m]]))
  )

best_model <- model_comparison$model[which.min(model_comparison$cv_wape)]
best_fit <- fits[[best_model]]
best_spec <- spec_of(best_model)

write_rds(
  list(
    fits = fits, cv_predictions = cv_predictions, fold_parameters = fold_parameters,
    fold = fold, best_model = best_model, bus_col = bus_col
  ),
  file.path(rds_dir, "model_fits.rds"),
  compress = "gz"
)

model_comparison |>
  mutate(
    lambda = round(lambda, 2),
    across(c(in_sample_wape, cv_wape), fmt_pct)
  ) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Description", "Parameters", "λ", "In-sample WAPE", "Cross-validated WAPE"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-model-ladder
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "In-sample and cross-validated error for each model"
#| fig-alt: "Dot plot with one row per model. Each row shows the in-sample WAPE and the cross-validated WAPE, joined by a line; a longer line means the model does worse on unseen stations."
#| fig-width: 8

model_comparison |>
  mutate(model_label = factor(str_c(model, ": ", label), levels = rev(str_c(model, ": ", label)))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(in_sample_wape, cv_wape), names_to = "measure", values_to = "wape") |>
  mutate(measure = if_else(measure == "cv_wape", "Cross-validated", "In-sample")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = wape, y = model_label)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = model_label), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = measure), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("In-sample" = "#86b6ef", "Cross-validated" = "#1c5cab")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA)) +

```

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr has_od
Each step down the ladder adds information to the model. A step is worth keeping when the dark point, the error on stations the model never saw, moves left. A wide gap between the two points would mean the model fits today's stations better than it predicts new ones.
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-fold-stability
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Parameter estimates across the five cross-validation folds, selected model"
#| fig-alt: "Small-multiple strip plots, one per parameter of the selected model. Light points are the five fold estimates and the dark bar is the estimate from all stations."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
parameter_labels <- c(
  lambda = "Distance decay (λ)",
  gamma_lines = "Rail lines (γ lines)",
  gamma_bus = "Bus stops (γ bus)",
  delta_lrt = "LRT-only (δ)",
  log_w_floor = "Workplace weight (log ω floor)",
  log_w_poi = "Activity weight (log ω POI)"
)

fold_parameters |>
  filter(model == best_model) |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter_labels[parameter], levels = parameter_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = 0)) +
  geom_point(color = "#86b6ef", size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(
    data = tibble(
      parameter = factor(parameter_labels[names(best_fit$theta)], levels = parameter_labels),
      value = unname(best_fit$theta)
    ),
    shape = "|", size = 10, color = "#0d366b"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  labs(x = "Estimate (bar: all stations; points: each fold)", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "#e1e0d9"),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "lines")
  )
```

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr has_od
Each fold leaves out one-fifth of the network, so a parameter whose five points sit close to the bar does not depend on any one part of Singapore. A parameter whose points spread widely is weakly identified, and predictions that lean on it, such as the extra-line uplift in section 6.5, deserve more caution.
```

```{r}
#| label: stability-commentary
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
stability <- fold_parameters |>
  filter(model == best_model) |>
  group_by(parameter) |>
  summarise(low = min(value), high = max(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(label = parameter_labels[parameter], sign_flips = low < 0 & high > 0)

lambda_range <- stability |> filter(parameter == "lambda")
flipping <- stability |> filter(sign_flips)

cat(str_glue(
  "In this fit, distance decay stays between {round(lambda_range$low, 2)} and {round(lambda_range$high, 2)} ",
  "across the five folds, so the strong preference for nearby stations does not come from one region. ",
  if (nrow(flipping) > 0) {
    str_c(
      "The estimate for ", str_c(str_to_lower(flipping$label), collapse = " and "),
      " changes sign between folds, so that feature adds little reliable information."
    )
  } else {
    "No parameter changes sign between folds."
  }
))
```

```{r}
  )

ggplot(error_by_type, aes(x = percent_error, y = station_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.4) +

  ) +
```

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr has_od
A group whose median bar sits away from zero is systematically over- or under-predicted. That matters for the scenarios: seven of the new stations become interchanges, and every new station is a single-line MRT stop, so bias in those two groups carries straight into the estimates in Part 6.
```

```{r}
#| label: bias-commentary
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
type_bias <- error_by_type |>
  group_by(station_type) |>
  summarise(median_error = median(percent_error), .groups = "drop")

describe_bias <- function(type) {
  m <- type_bias$median_error[type_bias$station_type == type]
  if (abs(m) < 0.01) return("close to unbiased")
  str_c(fmt_pct(abs(m), 0), if (m < 0) " under-predicted" else " over-predicted")
}

cat(str_glue(
  "Here the median interchange is {describe_bias('Interchange')}, the median single-line MRT station ",
  "{describe_bias('Single-line MRT')}, and the median LRT stop {describe_bias('LRT only')}."
))
```

```{r}
#| label: selection-commentary

best_row <- model_comparison |> filter(model == best_model)
m0_row <- model_comparison |> filter(model == "M0")

held_out_errors <- dest_existing |>
  mutate(error = cv_predictions[[best_model]] - avg_weekday_entries)
under <- held_out_errors |> slice_min(error, n = 4)
over <- held_out_errors |> slice_max(error, n = 3)

cat(str_glue(
  "The selected model, {best_row$model} ({best_row$label}), predicts held-out stations with a ",
  "weighted absolute percentage error of {fmt_pct(best_row$cv_wape)}, against {fmt_pct(m0_row$cv_wape)} ",
  "for distance alone. Its decay exponent is {round(best_row$lambda, 2)}: a station 400 m away pulls ",
  "{fmt_pct((400 / 100)^(-best_row$lambda))} as strongly as one 100 m away, other things equal. ",
  "The largest shortfalls are at {str_c(under$station_label, collapse = ', ')}, central workplace ",
  "stations whose riders include commuters and visitors from outside the modelled demand. ",
  "The largest over-predictions are at {str_c(over$station_label, collapse = ', ')}."
))
```

# Part 6: Expanded Network Scenarios

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr "!has_od"
::: callout-note
This part applies the calibrated model and runs once the passenger files are added to `data/`.
:::
```

## 6.1 Four network scenarios

The selected model is applied, with its fitted parameters, to four networks: the existing network, the JRL added, CRL Phase 1 added, and both added. Total predicted entries are the same in every scenario, because the model redistributes a fixed number of trips.

```{r}
#| label: run-scenarios
#| eval: !expr has_od
run_scenario <- function(scenario, uplift = TRUE) {
  dest <- scenario_destinations(scenario, uplift)
  shares <- huff_shares(
    log(dist_mat[, dest$station_id]),
    log_attraction(best_fit$theta, dest, best_spec, bus_col),
    best_fit$theta[["lambda"]]
  )
  dest$predicted <- best_fit$kappa * drop(crossprod(shares, demand_vector(best_fit$theta, best_spec)))
  list(dest = dest, shares = shares)
}

scenario_runs <- map(set_names(names(scenario_lines)), run_scenario)

scenario_results <- map(names(scenario_runs), \(s) {
  scenario_runs[[s]]$dest |> mutate(scenario = s)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

write_rds(scenario_results, file.path(rds_dir, "scenario_results.rds"), compress = "gz")

scenario_summary <- scenario_results |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    total_entries = sum(predicted),
    new_station_entries = sum(predicted[station_type == "new_alternative"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    new_station_share = new_station_entries / total_entries,
    scenario = factor(scenario_labels[scenario], levels = scenario_labels)
  ) |>
  arrange(scenario)

scenario_summary |>
  mutate(across(c(total_entries, new_station_entries), fmt_num), new_station_share = fmt_pct(new_station_share)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Scenario", "Total weekday entries", "Entries at new stations", "Share at new stations"))
```

## 6.2 Busy and quiet new stations

A new station is flagged as quiet if its prediction is below the 10th percentile of observed entries at existing MRT stations. LRT stops are left out of the comparison because they are small feeder stations, while every new station is on an MRT line.

```{r}
#| label: fig-new-stations
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Predicted weekday entries at the 29 new stations, both lines added"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the 29 new stations ranked by predicted weekday entries, coloured by line, with a reference line at the quiet-station threshold."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
quiet_threshold <- quantile(observed[!dest_existing$is_lrt], 0.10)

new_station_results <- scenario_runs$both$dest |>
  filter(station_type == "new_alternative") |>
  mutate(quiet = predicted < quiet_threshold)

new_station_results |>
  mutate(station_label = fct_reorder(station_label, predicted)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = predicted, y = station_label, fill = line)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = quiet_threshold, color = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = quiet_threshold, y = 1, label = " Quiet threshold", hjust = 0, size = 3.2, color = ink_secondary) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = line_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted weekday entries", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

