```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_od
new_station_results |>
  filter(quiet) |>
  arrange(predicted) |>
  transmute(station = station_label, line, predicted_entries = fmt_num(predicted), bus_stops_400m = bus_400) |>
  kable()
```

## 6.3 Impact on existing stations

```{r}
#| label: fig-losses
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Existing stations losing the most predicted entries, both lines added"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the ten existing stations with the largest predicted fall in weekday entries when both lines are added."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
station_change <- scenario_runs$existing$dest |>
  select(station_id, station_label, existing = predicted) |>
  inner_join(scenario_runs$both$dest |> select(station_id, both = predicted), by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(change = both - existing, change_pct = change / existing)

biggest_losses <- station_change |>
  slice_min(change, n = 10)

biggest_losses |>
  mutate(station_label = fct_reorder(station_label, change, .desc = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = -change, y = station_label)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#e34948", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_pct(change_pct)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2, color = ink_secondary) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Predicted weekday entries lost (label: % change)", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Which existing lines give up the riders? Each station's change is shared equally among the lines it serves and then summed by line.

```{r}
#| label: fig-line-impact
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Net change in predicted weekday entries by existing line, both lines added"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the net change in predicted weekday entries for each existing MRT and LRT line when both new lines open, with the largest loss at the top."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
line_names <- c(
  NS = "North-South", EW = "East-West", NE = "North East", CC = "Circle",
  DT = "Downtown", TE = "Thomson-East Coast",
  BPLRT = "Bukit Panjang LRT", SLRT = "Sengkang LRT", PLRT = "Punggol LRT"
)

station_line_share <- station_codes |>
  mutate(line = line_of(code)) |>
  distinct(station_id, line) |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
  ungroup()

line_impact <- station_change |>
  inner_join(station_line_share, by = "station_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(line) |>
  summarise(net_change = sum(change * weight), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(line_name = fct_reorder(line_names[line], net_change, .desc = TRUE))

ggplot(line_impact, aes(x = net_change, y = line_name)) +
  geom_col(fill = if_else(line_impact$net_change < 0, "#e34948", "#2a78d6"), width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Net change in predicted weekday entries", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{asis}
#| echo: !expr has_od
Red bars are lines whose stations lose entries overall; blue bars gain, usually because their stations become upgraded interchanges. The pattern shows which existing services will carry fewer first-leg riders, and so where feeder buses and train frequencies could be rebalanced.
```

```{r}
#| label: line-commentary
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
largest_line_loss <- line_impact |> slice_min(net_change, n = 1)

cat(str_glue(
  "In this run the {largest_line_loss$line_name} Line loses the most, about ",
  "{fmt_num(abs(largest_line_loss$net_change), -2)} predicted weekday entries."
))
```

## 6.4 Catchment shifts

A subzone's preferred station is the one that captures the largest share of its residential demand. The map shows the subzones whose preferred station changes when both lines are added; hover for the station before and after.

```{r}
#| label: catchment-shift
#| eval: !expr has_od
home_rows <- origins$origin_type == "home"

preferred_station <- function(run) {
  by_subzone <- rowsum(run$shares[home_rows, ] * origins$home_m2[home_rows], origins$subzone_id[home_rows])
  tibble(
    subzone_id = rownames(by_subzone),
    station_id = colnames(run$shares)[max.col(by_subzone, ties.method = "first")]
  )
}

label_of <- setNames(stations$station_label, stations$station_id)

catchment_shift <- preferred_station(scenario_runs$existing) |>
  rename(before = station_id) |>
  inner_join(preferred_station(scenario_runs$both) |> rename(after = station_id), by = "subzone_id") |>
  mutate(changed = before != after, before_label = label_of[before], after_label = label_of[after])

catchment_map <- subzones |>
  inner_join(catchment_shift, by = "subzone_id") |>
  st_transform(4326)

leaflet(catchment_map) |>
  # Esri's light grey basemap needs no API key (CARTO tiles now require one)
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = if_else(catchment_map$changed, report_colors[["New alternative"]], "#d9d8d0"),
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    weight = 0.6,
    label = str_c(catchment_map$subzone, ": ", catchment_map$before_label, " → ", catchment_map$after_label)
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    colors = c(report_colors[["New alternative"]], "#d9d8d0"),
    labels = c("Preferred station changes", "No change"),
    position = "bottomright"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: catchment-table
#| eval: !expr has_od
catchment_shift |>
  filter(changed) |>
  count(before_label, sort = TRUE, name = "subzones_lost") |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Station losing subzones", "Subzones lost"))
```

## 6.5 Interchange sensitivity

Upgraded interchanges gain riders for two reasons: they stay close to residents, and the model gives them one more line. Rerunning with the extra-line uplift switched off separates the two.

```{r}
#| label: fig-uplift
#| eval: !expr has_od
#| fig-cap: "Predicted entries at upgraded interchanges with and without the extra-line uplift"
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell chart for the seven upgraded interchanges, comparing predicted entries without the extra line to predictions with it."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
no_uplift <- run_scenario("both", uplift = FALSE)

uplift_test <- scenario_runs$existing$dest |>
  filter(!is.na(upgraded_by)) |>
  select(station_id, station_label, upgraded_by, existing = predicted) |>
  inner_join(no_uplift$dest |> select(station_id, without_uplift = predicted), by = "station_id") |>
  inner_join(scenario_runs$both$dest |> select(station_id, with_uplift = predicted), by = "station_id")

uplift_test |>
  mutate(station_label = fct_reorder(station_label, with_uplift)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = station_label)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = without_uplift, xend = with_uplift, yend = station_label), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = without_uplift, color = "Without extra line"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = with_uplift, color = "With extra line"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Without extra line" = "#86b6ef", "With extra line" = "#1c5cab")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted weekday entries, both lines added", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: uplift-table
#| eval: !expr has_od
uplift_test |>
  transmute(
    station = station_label, new_line = upgraded_by,
    existing = fmt_num(existing), without_uplift = fmt_num(without_uplift),
    with_uplift = fmt_num(with_uplift)
  ) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Station", "New line code", "Existing network", "Both lines, no uplift", "Both lines, with uplift"))
```

The gap between the two points is the part of an interchange's prediction that rests on the modelling assumption that an extra line makes a station more attractive. Where it is wide, the prediction depends heavily on that assumption.

# Part 7: Accessibility and Equity Analysis

This part does not use the Huff model. It measures how much closer HDB buildings are to a station once both lines open. Open stations are those with recorded entries, or, if passenger data is absent, those provisionally treated as open in section 2.2.

## 7.1 Distance savings

```{r}
#| label: distance-savings
home_dist <- dist_mat[origins$origin_type == "home", ]
nearest_m <- function(scenario) {
  apply(home_dist[, scenario_destinations(scenario)$station_id, drop = FALSE], 1, min)
}

home_access <- homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(origin_id, subzone_id, subzone, planning_area, home_m2) |>
  mutate(
    before_m = nearest_m("existing"),
    after_m = nearest_m("both"),
    saving_m = before_m - after_m
  )

write_rds(home_access, file.path(rds_dir, "home_access.rds"), compress = "gz")

home_access |>
  summarise(
    buildings = n(),
    buildings_closer = sum(saving_m > 0),
    median_saving_if_closer_m = median(saving_m[saving_m > 0]),
    gaining_over_500m = sum(saving_m > 500)
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-nearest-ecdf
#| fig-cap: "Share of HDB buildings within a given distance of a station"
#| fig-alt: "Two cumulative curves of distance to the nearest station. The curve with both lines added sits above the existing-network curve."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
home_access |>
  select(before_m, after_m) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "scenario", values_to = "nearest_m") |>
  mutate(scenario = if_else(scenario == "before_m", "Existing network", "Both lines added")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = nearest_m, color = scenario)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(400, 800, 1200), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.8, pad = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Existing network" = "#898781", "Both lines added" = "#2a78d6")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma(), breaks = seq(0, 2000, 400)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 2000)) +
  labs(x = "Straight-line distance to nearest station (m)", y = "Share of HDB buildings") +
  theme_report()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-saving-by-line
#| fig-cap: "Distance saved by HDB buildings that gain a closer station, by the line that serves them"
#| fig-alt: "Two histograms of distance saved, one for buildings whose new nearest station is on the Jurong Region Line and one for the Cross Island Line."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
both_ids <- scenario_destinations("both")$station_id
new_nearest <- both_ids[max.col(-home_dist[, both_ids], ties.method = "first")]

saving_by_line <- home_access |>
  mutate(new_nearest = new_nearest) |>
  filter(saving_m > 0) |>
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(stations) |> select(station_id, line), by = c(new_nearest = "station_id")) |>
  mutate(line = if_else(line == "JRL", "Jurong Region Line", "Cross Island Line Phase 1"))

saving_counts <- saving_by_line |>
  count(line) |>
  mutate(facet_label = str_c(line, " (", fmt_num(n), " buildings)"))

saving_by_line |>
  left_join(saving_counts, by = "line") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = saving_m, fill = line)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, boundary = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~facet_label, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = unname(line_colors["JRL"]), "Cross Island Line Phase 1" = unname(line_colors["CRL"]))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma(), breaks = seq(0, 3000, 500)) +
  labs(x = "Distance saved to the nearest station (m)", y = "HDB buildings") +
  theme_report() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The JRL brings `r fmt_num(saving_counts$n[saving_counts$line == "Jurong Region Line"])` HDB buildings closer to a station and CRL Phase 1 brings `r fmt_num(saving_counts$n[saving_counts$line == "Cross Island Line Phase 1"])`, with similar typical savings of about half a kilometre. Both histograms have a long right tail: `r fmt_num(sum(saving_by_line$saving_m > 1000))` buildings save more than a kilometre, which is the difference between walking and needing a feeder bus.

## 7.2 Subzone coverage

Coverage is the share of HDB footprint, as a proxy for flats, within 400 m, 800 m and 1,200 m of a station.

```{r}
#| label: coverage
coverage <- expand_grid(threshold_m = c(400, 800, 1200), scenario = c("existing", "both")) |>
  mutate(
    footprint_share = map2_dbl(threshold_m, scenario, \(t, s) {
      d <- if (s == "existing") home_access$before_m else home_access$after_m
      sum(home_access$home_m2[d <= t]) / sum(home_access$home_m2)
    }),
    building_share = map2_dbl(threshold_m, scenario, \(t, s) {
      d <- if (s == "existing") home_access$before_m else home_access$after_m
      mean(d <= t)
    })
  )

coverage |>
  mutate(
    scenario = scenario_labels[scenario],
    threshold_m = str_c("Within ", fmt_num(threshold_m), " m"),
    across(c(footprint_share, building_share), fmt_pct)
  ) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Distance", "Scenario", "Share of HDB footprint", "Share of HDB buildings"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pa-coverage
#| fig-cap: "HDB footprint within 800 m of a station, by planning area"
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell chart of the planning areas whose 800-metre coverage changes, comparing the existing network with both lines added."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
pa_coverage <- home_access |>
  group_by(planning_area) |>
  summarise(
    before = sum(home_m2[before_m <= 800]) / sum(home_m2),
    after = sum(home_m2[after_m <= 800]) / sum(home_m2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(after - before > 0.005)

pa_coverage |>
  mutate(planning_area = fct_reorder(planning_area, after - before)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = planning_area)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = before, xend = after, yend = planning_area), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = before, color = "Existing network"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = after, color = "Both lines added"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Existing network" = "#898781", "Both lines added" = "#2a78d6"), breaks = c("Existing network", "Both lines added")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Share of HDB footprint within 800 m of a station", y = NULL) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Coverage within 800 m rises by more than half a percentage point in `r nrow(pa_coverage)` planning areas. Tengah gains the most, from almost no HDB within 800 m of a station to `r fmt_pct(pa_coverage$after[pa_coverage$planning_area == "Tengah"], 0)`. Serangoon, Pasir Ris and the Jurong areas also gain sharply, while Hougang and Tampines still have a quarter or more of their HDB footprint beyond 800 m.

```{r}
#| label: fig-saving-map
#| fig-cap: "Average distance saved per subzone, both lines added"
#| fig-alt: "Choropleth of subzones with HDB housing, where darker blue means a larger footprint-weighted average reduction in distance to the nearest station. The gains concentrate along the two new lines."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
subzone_saving <- home_access |>
  group_by(subzone_id) |>
  summarise(
    mean_saving_m = weighted.mean(saving_m, home_m2),
    share_beyond_800m_after = sum(home_m2[after_m > 800]) / sum(home_m2),
    footprint_beyond_800m_ha = sum(home_m2[after_m > 800]) / 1e4,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(x = subzones, by = "subzone_id")

map_base() +
  tm_shape(subzone_saving) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "mean_saving_m",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
      breaks = c(0, 1, 50, 200, 500, Inf),
      values = c("#ffffff", blue_ramp[2:5]),
      labels = c("No change", "1 to 50", "50 to 200", "200 to 500", "Over 500")
    ),
    fill.legend = map_legend("Average saving (m)"),
    col = "#d9d8d0",
    lwd = 0.3
  ) +
  map_finish()
```

```{r}
#| label: access-commentary
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cov_800 <- coverage |> filter(threshold_m == 800)

cat(str_glue(
  "With both lines, the share of HDB footprint within 800 m of a station rises from ",
  "{fmt_pct(cov_800$footprint_share[cov_800$scenario == 'existing'])} to ",
  "{fmt_pct(cov_800$footprint_share[cov_800$scenario == 'both'])}. ",
  "{fmt_num(sum(home_access$saving_m > 0))} of {fmt_num(nrow(home_access))} HDB buildings get closer ",
  "to a station, and for them the median saving is {fmt_num(median(home_access$saving_m[home_access$saving_m > 0]))} m. ",
  "The gains are concentrated in subzones along the two new lines; elsewhere the nearest station does not change."
))
```

## 7.3 Equity for older residents

The planned equity test groups subzones into quartiles by their share of residents aged 65 and over, then compares distances to the nearest station. That needs SingStat population by age, which is not in this study's data, so the test is not run.

Instead, the table lists the subzones with the most HDB footprint still beyond 800 m of a station after both lines open. These are the estates where walking routes and feeder buses matter most, whatever their residents' ages.

```{r}
#| label: beyond-800
far_subzones <- subzone_saving |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(footprint_beyond_800m_ha > 0) |>
  slice_max(footprint_beyond_800m_ha, n = 10)

far_subzones |>
  transmute(
    subzone, planning_area,
    footprint_beyond_800m_ha = round(footprint_beyond_800m_ha, 1),
    share_of_subzone = fmt_pct(share_beyond_800m_after)
  ) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Subzone", "Planning area", "HDB footprint beyond 800 m (ha)", "Share of subzone footprint"))
```

# Part 8: Findings, Limitations and Recommendations

```{r}
#| label: summary-metrics
#| echo: false
cov_800_before <- cov_800$footprint_share[cov_800$scenario == "existing"]
cov_800_after <- cov_800$footprint_share[cov_800$scenario == "both"]
far_text <- str_c(head(far_subzones$subzone, 3), collapse = ", ")

if (has_od) {
  wape_text <- str_c(fmt_pct(min(model_comparison$cv_wape)), " (", best_model, ")")
  capture_text <- fmt_pct(scenario_summary$new_station_share[scenario_summary$scenario == scenario_labels[["both"]]])
  quiet_text <- if (any(new_station_results$quiet)) {
    str_c(
      str_c(new_station_results$station_label[new_station_results$quiet], collapse = ", "),
      ", below ", fmt_num(quiet_threshold, -2), " weekday entries"
    )
  } else {
    str_c("none below ", fmt_num(quiet_threshold, -2), " weekday entries, though the lowest estimates still deserve a check")
  }
  loser_text <- str_c(head(biggest_losses$station_label, 3), collapse = ", ")
} else {
  wape_text <- "pending passenger data"
  capture_text <- "pending passenger data"
  quiet_text <- "to be identified once passenger data is added"
  loser_text <- "to be identified once passenger data is added"
}
```

## 8.1 Key metrics

| Metric | Value |
|----|----|
| Cross-validated WAPE of the selected model | `r wape_text` |
| Share of weekday trips captured by the 29 new stations | `r capture_text` |
| HDB footprint within 800 m of a station, existing network | `r fmt_pct(cov_800_before)` |
| HDB footprint within 800 m of a station, both lines added | `r fmt_pct(cov_800_after)` |

## 8.2 Limitations

- Distances are straight lines and ignore walking routes, so stations across rivers, expressways or industrial land are closer on paper than on foot.
- The model redistributes today's trips and cannot show new ones induced by the lines.
- Only entries are modelled. Transfers within the network are not, so a station's figure counts only riders who enter there.
- Demand relies on proxies. Residential demand is HDB footprint, which ignores building height, private housing and non-resident workers. Workplace demand is OpenStreetMap floor area and activity counts, whose completeness varies across the island.
- With no age data, the equity test for older residents could not be run.
- Bus stops and buildings near proposed stations reflect current conditions, not those when the lines open.

## 8.3 Planning priorities

- Verify quiet stations before confirming opening plans. Stations predicted to be quiet: `r quiet_text`. Local evidence on planned housing and jobs should be gathered first, since the model cannot see future development.
- Redesign feeder buses around stations that lose catchment. Stations expected to lose the most entries: `r loser_text`. Their bus routes should be reviewed so that riders who switch are well served.
- Improve walking and feeder links in estates that stay far from rail. `r far_text` keep the most HDB footprint beyond 800 m of a station even after both lines open. They should be prioritised for walking-path and feeder improvements.
